caption:
Your traffic dropped during the core update, so it must be the update. Right? 🎃

Before you blame Google, check which searches left. In Search Console, open Performance, choose Compare in the date filter at the top, pick the last two weeks against the two before, and click the Queries tab (not Pages). If every search that lost clicks is a seasonal one, like Halloween cupcakes, people simply stopped searching for it. Google's own guide lists seasonality as one of the main causes of a traffic drop. Want to be sure? Set the date range to 16 months and see if the same dip happens every year.

Send this to the friend who blames every drop on the update.

What seasonal post fooled you this year? (Maya and Floey are from Flowra.)
topic: Google dropped Maya overnight in the middle of the core update. The update didn't do it: Halloween ended.
editorNotes: The hook frame can't be drawn as written. It asks for a wide shot of Maya panicking, a full screenInsert chart and the phone notification all on screen at t=0, with none of them overlapping. screenInsert is a screen-space cutaway with a fixed layout, so the animator can't shrink it into a corner of a wide shot. Pick one opening frame. Either open on the chart insert already falling, with the notification down, and cut to wide/mayaTight panic by the end of the first sentence. Or open wide on Maya with a bad number pill by her head, with the notification down, and drop the chart.

The button line 'Same panic, next October.' sounds like a tagline, not something Floey would say out loud. It also lands right after the real laugh ('My coffee's cold.') and doesn't top it, so the ending fizzles. Floey needs a spoken, smug-warm last line that clearly caps the scene. The brief's 'See you next October.' is the kind of line that works. Or end on the coffee and Maya's look, and give Floey a short callback like 'You're welcome.'

(polish) The delivery notes contradict each other on the coffee line. 'My coffee's cold.' is tagged worried, but the visual says flat and deadpan, staring into the mug. A worried read kills the joke. Change the emotion so the voice comes out flat (or as close to flat as the emotion set allows), or drop 'worried' from the direction.

(polish) Some of the tip isn't backed by the brief. 'Then Queries, not Pages.' tells viewers to ignore Pages, but the brief's source says to click all the tabs (queries, URLs, countries, devices). 'Then check Queries.' or 'Then look at Queries.' stays true and is still one tip. Read aloud, 'Compare the last two weeks with the two before' is fine for Floey.

(polish) The notification 'Google: core update rolling out' shows Google itself pushing an alert to Maya's phone, which Google doesn't do. Use a sender like 'SEO news' or 'Search Status' so the joke doesn't rest on a false detail. It also says the notification is 'already slid down' at t=0 but plays a 'ding in the first frames'. Either it slides in during the first half second with the ding, or it's already down and stays silent.

(polish) In the doubt beat, Maya uses pointL 'at the laptop'. pointL points screen left, which is where Floey sits on the lid, so it will read as Maya blaming Floey. Use facepalm, panic or shrug, or point if the screen is meant.

(polish) Floey's listening acting repeats: a slow blink and head tilt in the reframe, then 'a slow head tilt and a long slow blink' again in the doubt beat. Give her a different reaction the second time (a tongue flick, a turn away to preen, a tiny chip).

(polish) Maya reads the three falling rows, but nobody notices the banana bread and lemon drizzle rows holding steady. Those rows are what proves Google didn't punish the whole blog. Either let the hi ring or a quick look land on '+6' before 'Oh.', or give Maya a two-word aside so the viewer gets the proof as well as the pattern. The spoken 'Halloween cupcakes' also differs slightly from the row label 'halloween cupcake ideas'. That's fine if the caption matches what she says.

(polish) Check the mayaTight frame for 'Oh.'. With her face filling the frame, a '!' mark above her head may sit outside the safe area (y 220 or below the top 200 px covered by Instagram) or get cut off. Nudge the shot or put the mark beside her head.

(polish) The brief's best relatable detail, 'and Bing still loves me', has been dropped. It's what made the drop feel personal, and it's the exact situation from the forum thread. Consider bringing it back into Maya's doubt line instead of 'Google hates me' (or alongside it, kept short).
